title: The `while` Loop: Conditional Repetition ⏳
description: Repeat code as long as a condition holds true. Read files line‑by‑line like a pro.

slides.title: `while` – Loop While True ✅
slides.content:
## Keep Going Until Condition Fails

The `while` loop executes its block as long as the test command returns success (exit code 0).

Syntax:
```bash
while [ condition ]; do
   commands
done
```
Each iteration re‑checks the condition.

slides.title: Count to 5
slides.codeSnippet:
count=1
while [ $count -le 5 ]; do
  echo "Count: $count"
  count=$((count + 1))
done

quizData.question: What must you do inside a `while` loop to avoid an infinite loop?

options.text: Change the loop variable or condition so it eventually becomes false

quizData.explanation: If the condition never changes, the loop runs forever. You must update variables involved in the condition.

slides.title: Reading Files Line‑by‑Line 📖
slides.content:
## The Classic `while read` Pattern

To process a file line by line without word splitting issues, use:
```bash
while IFS= read -r line; do
   echo "$line"
done < "$filename"
```
- `IFS=` – prevents stripping of leading/trailing whitespace.
- `-r` – prevents backslash interpretation.
- `< "$filename"` redirects the file into the loop.

slides.title: Read /etc/hosts
slides.content: Print lines from a system file:
slides.codeSnippet:
while IFS= read -r line; do
  echo "Line: $line"
done < /etc/hosts

quizData.question: Which option to `read` prevents backslash escapes from being interpreted?
quizData.explanation: `-r` stands for raw input, leaving backslashes alone.

slides.title: Infinite Loops & User Input 🔄
slides.content:
## `while true` – The Never‑ending Loop

Sometimes you want a loop that runs until the user quits:
```bash
while true; do
   read -p "Enter command (quit to exit): " cmd
   if [ "$cmd" = "quit" ]; then
      break
   fi
   echo "You typed: $cmd"
done
```

slides.title: Simple REPL
slides.codeSnippet:
while true; do
  read -p "> " input
  case $input in
    quit) break ;;
    *) echo "Echo: $input" ;;
  esac
done

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: You can read multiple variables from a line: `while read col1 col2 col3; do ... done < data.csv`. The last variable gets the remainder.
